description: One set of scenarios, run three ways. See README.md.

scenarios.why: A client must be able to ask what a node supports before assuming a feature exists.
Insert, read back, and a missing document that is absent rather than an error.
Omitting a limit returns 100 documents, not the collection. A client that hides this moves the surprise.
The walk sees every document exactly once, in order.
A final page that is exactly full still carries a token. A walk that stops when the token stops arriving reads one page too few.
A sort other than _id ascending cannot be paged, and the client says so rather than letting the second page fail.
The specification claimed creation was idempotent and the server has always returned 409. Found by this suite, so it is a scenario now.
A refusal arrives with its code and retry class, not as a status a caller has to interpret.
A client holding credentials survives its own token expiring, without the caller noticing.
A dead address in front of a live one must not stop the client — including at login, which is the first request it makes.
`elsewhere` says this node did not answer, not that the work did not happen. A helpful retry would apply an insert twice.
Events arrive, in order, with the post-image when asked for.
A token is a position with no server state, so a stream started from it sees what the first missed.
A dropped collection ends its streams rather than leaving them open and silent.
Ids are derived from the name, so a recreated collection reuses one. Its predecessor's entries are not its history.
A token from before a drop names a position in a collection that no longer exists. Refused rather than moved forward silently, because the gap is real.
